answer: Tie each identity to one physical sensor, say a weather station whose signed readings form a living atlas of local conditions. A gale recorded by one station must match its neighbours' readings, and a voyage of data over weeks must stay time- and location-consistent, so a sybil farmer cannot spin up a thousand fake identities from one laptop: each needs real hardware, installed somewhere, kept running. Limit: honest agents without a sensor are locked out, and a clever attacker can still replay genuine readings from one device across clones until cross-checks catch the duplication.
